history.summary: Ancient cave temple built in 1553 CE by Maharaja Bahadur Singh of Kullu, in four-tiered pagoda style (24 m tall wooden shikhara) amid the Dhungiri cedar forest. It is built over the rock where Hidimba, wife of Bhima (Mahabharata), is said to have meditated and attained goddess status; the sanctum holds the worshipped rock, not an idol, and a small shrine to her son Ghatotkacha stands ~70 m away. CORRECTION: CSV town 'Kullu' is wrong; the temple is at Manali (Kullu district), ~40 km north of Kullu town. CONFLICT: travel guides report timings 8:00 AM-6:00 PM, while some listings report 6:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify locally. Coordinates from Wikipedia/GeoHack.

name: Hidimba Devi Temple
town_description: Manali is a high-altitude Himalayan resort town in Kullu district on the Beas river, ~40 km north of Kullu town. It is a major tourist hub and gateway to Solang valley, Rohtang pass and Parvati valley treks.

travel.airport: Bhuntar (Kullu-Manali) Airport, ~50 km south of Manali
travel.railway: Nearest narrow-gauge railhead: Joginder Nagar (~165 km); nearest broad-gauge: Chandigarh (~310 km)
travel.road: 2 km from Mall Road, Manali (5-10 min drive or 25-30 min uphill walk); well-connected by road to Chandigarh (~310 km) and Delhi

visitor_information.opening_hours: 8:00 AM-6:00 PM daily per travel guides; some listings report 6:00 AM-8:00 PM - verify locally
